October 9 (later) **— 3.2.17 (91) `9dd272e8`, automatic updates, PSP and Switch.**
Owner decisions: personal debug-signed builds only (no release signing); every
install must update itself from GitHub; theme changes limited to polish; the
Thor must keep behaving as it does. Candidate
`lucent-3.2.17-lsfg-framegen-qualification-9dd272e8310922b4cdd1ac9d4c6596b261a25032a53d9f4e200964e6687a910b.apk`
(pinned; 25332 is the rollback). Same natives as 25332; changes:
`UpdateManager` checks GitHub releases/latest on every build at startup and
again (6 h) when the library is shown, downloads and verifies (digest, package,
higher versionCode, same signer), never interrupts gameplay (the install waits
for the library) and reuses a verified download; new loop video
(`branding/loading-fusion`, video 3e50fc59); footer legends fit narrow phone
windows (compact set, then shrink) while wide windows such as the Thor render
exactly as before (`tools/tests/test_footer_legend_fit.py`).
Owned PSP/Switch inputs were streamed read-only from the Thor
(`qa/.../current-build-survey/thor-input-*.json`). PSP (Castlevania Dracula X
Chronicles, LittleBigPlanet) on the clean phone: discovery, boot, gameplay
(move/whip/jump; analog-stick walk), pause/resume, exit with checkpoint. Switch
(Mega Man 11): keys + 238 firmware files installed by the app; the simulator's
host Vulkan (MoltenVK) lacks geometryShader/logicOp/wideLines so Eden cannot start
there; with `-gpu lavapipe` it boots, menus/New Game work and the in-game tutorial
is reached at ~1 fps (software). On the Thor (Adreno, 3.2.17 installed with data
preserved, rollback `adb install -r -d` to e8aefd6a possible) Mega Man 11 plays at
60 fps (run, jump, buster, pause menu). Publication: the signed-in GitHub account
can push only to the fork; a release on `wildonrio/pegasus-lucent` (the updater's
channel) needs the owner account.

touch into an ANR and blocked the pause menu. (2) BlastEm NEW_CORE frame-end
cycle rebase run from inside `m68k_execute` left its local target_cycle ~2^32
ahead, so retro_run never returned (Sonic 2 Aquatic Ruin demo; reproduced on
device twice and deterministically on a Mac harness). Patch
`engines/patches/blastem-new-core-frame-end-rebase-hang.patch`; core e479c08d
from two byte-identical clean builds; Phase 1 lock updated and passing. Device
soak ran 71k frames past the reproduced freeze frame, then gameplay/exit.
(3) Bounded wedged-exit frontend restart (15 s) when Exit cannot quiesce a
core; host-tested; normal exits verified not to trigger it.

October 6 **01:02 — private native/Java exit reporting implemented and tested.**
`PrivateDiagnosticsExitRecovery` now matches an unfinished opted-in session to
Android's own recorded process-exit category. It never reads trace streams or
descriptions. Only schema/build/system/event/bucket can be transmitted. The
temporary process PID and session time are local matching data, not device IDs
and not report fields. Normal close and opting out discard the local marker;
late callbacks cannot inherit new consent or erase a replacement session.

## Timing math

Keep these quantities distinct:

- `C`: original declared core clock, verified against retired guest ticks.
- `F`: the game's changing-image cadence, not the core callback rate.
- `r`: small gameplay-speed correction, also accounted for in audio.
- `R`: measured active physical display rate, not an Android refresh-rate vote.
- `m`: output multiplier, **1 or 2 only**.
- `n`: positive integer physical scans per output image.

The steady-stream contract is:

```text
C' = r × C
F' = r × F
O  = m × F'
R  = n × O
|r - 1| ≤ 0.0075
```

The existing 0.75% near-native correction budget is now enforced against the
original declared clock, never a previously slowed clock. It is a safety bound,
not a reason to alter an already matching game. Preserve the relationship between
guest ticks and image updates: a native 20 FPS game on a 60 Hz core stays on a
roughly 60 Hz core, **not a 20 Hz core**. Unknown/variable relationships need evidence;
do not invent a nominal rate from recent throughput.

Example: 60.1→60 uses `r = 60/60.1`, about -0.1664% gameplay speed. This fixes that
frequency mismatch only if the correction reaches the guest and the physical
presentation phase remains locked. Retimestamping without retiming the guest is
not equivalent.

For a nominal 120 Hz panel:

| Stable real-image FPS | Output | Multiplier | Scans/output image |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 60 | 120 | 2 | 1 |
| 40 | 40 direct | 1 | 3 |
| 30 | 60 | 2 | 2 |
| 24 | 24 direct | 1 | 5 |
| 20 | 40 | 2 | 3 |

On 60 Hz: 30→60 can generate; 60→60 and 20→20 stay direct. A true 40 Hz stream has
no uniform direct/doubled path on 60 Hz: choose a verified 120 Hz mode if available.
On a verified 80 Hz mode, 40→80 works. Do not assume Thor supports 80 Hz. Reject
40→80 on 120 Hz, fractional 40→60 conversion, and the old 3× paths 20→60 / 40→120.

Holding each output image for an equal number of panel scans is normal. At 20→40
on 120 Hz, each output occupies three scans. Those holds are **not** generated
frames. Static pairs and cut fallbacks cannot prove generated motion. A genuinely
incompatible 50 Hz game is not accelerated to 60; PAL conversion is outside this pass.

Discover each device's supported modes and verify the active mode after requesting
it. Use a common monotonic timeline, accumulated/rational deadlines and slow bounded
clock correction with hysteresis. Do not round FPS before planning, repeatedly
reanchor to hide drift, or reset failure totals on a new epoch. Frequency, physical
phase and guest-time progress each need measurement. Fractional measured-panel trim
is **not yet implemented across all native adapters**.

Android separates display-mode requests from rendering-loop synchronization:
[frame-rate API guidance](https://developer.android.com/media/optimize/performance/frame-rate).
Its [Frame Pacing library](https://developer.android.com/games/sdk/frame-pacing)
provides relevant presentation-time and synchronization mechanisms. A mode vote or
library integration alone does not qualify EmuFusion's source/output clocks.

## Useful generated frames

For adjacent retained real images `A(t0)` and `B(t1)`, produce at most one image,
`G((t0+t1)/2)`. It must represent midpoint motion and scene state, not copy A/B or
merely crossfade them. Missing/held periods cannot buy additional generated frames
between the same endpoints. Preserve pair identity across epoch changes.

True interpolation waits for the right endpoint and adds buffering latency. Measure
it; never silently substitute prediction. At 20 FPS, one source interval is 50 ms.
Cuts, newly revealed areas, transparencies, particles and HUD text need explicit
tests and conservative fallback. Optical flow cannot know all hidden content.

Required evidence:

1. **Exact runtime captures:** lossless full-resolution A/G/B from actual backend
   resources after GPU completion, joined to source IDs/timestamps, pair, phase,
   output/present ID, epoch and physical presentation result. Keep unmodified pixels;
   put labels outside them in contact sheets. Inspect typical and worst frames.
2. **Known reference:** withhold a true middle image from a deterministic high-rate
   recording or controlled scene. Feed only its neighbors through the same backend.
   Compare output with the hidden reference for pixel-art pans, subpixel motion,
   parallax, moving background/HUD, occlusion, thin geometry, particles and cuts.
   Compare motion error, edge/text damage and temporal consistency by region against
   copy-left, copy-right and blend baselines.

Different hashes, pixel-distance ratios near 0.5, and empty texture masks are not
proof of interpolation. Fix metrics, thresholds and regions before evaluation;
calibrate them against intentionally bad copies, blends, noise and warps. Require
improvement over the strongest simple baseline on the intended moving regions
without unacceptable local damage. Native-20/30 gameplay review without a true
reference is useful but not ground truth. Static/unobservable samples are
INSUFFICIENT, not automatic PASS.

Capture asynchronously in bounded bursts; retain exact resources until readback
retires. Qualify timing separately with readback disabled on the same replay and
settings; measure capture overhead. Android screen recording can omit 120 Hz
outputs and is not independent panel-scan proof.

## Adaptive GPU policy

Discover API/extensions, resource import/export/fences, GPU/driver, memory limits,
display modes and thermal state. Admit generation using **completed** GPU work and
emulator-plus-generator deadline margin, not model name, peak FPS, CPU enqueue
duration or shader time alone. Record explicit unsupported reasons.

Start within a quality envelope already validated by the image tests. Under
sustained pressure, lower interpolation resolution/work only within that envelope.
If no verified configuration fits, disable generation while preserving guest speed.
A renderer-only cap is allowed only where the emulator explicitly decouples drawing
from simulation and the retained source cadence remains qualified. Generic guest
underclocking is prohibited.

Retain session-wide missed deadlines, dropped frames, holds, Direct fallbacks,
allocation/fence failures and thermal transitions. Recovery requires consecutive
measured healthy work and backoff. Bad/missing timers cannot earn recovery. Test
chronic overload longer than the recovery horizon and avoid mode oscillation.
Fallback is a safety behavior, not proof that an overloaded emulator is smooth.

[`frame-generation-acceptance-v2.json`](../unified-android/tools/frame-generation-acceptance-v2.json).
All entries begin UNVERIFIED under this contract. Historical results do not transfer
to changed code/settings or an unidentified build.

Order: Switch → Wii U → 3DS → Wii → PS3 → PSP → DS → GameCube → GBA → PS2 → Dreamcast
→ GBC → N64 → PlayStation → SNES → Game Gear → GB → Mega Drive → NES. Then the extra
Windows/DOS route. Independent adapter blockers may be investigated in parallel.

Qualify Off, Built-in Alpha and private LSFG independently wherever supported.
Never silently substitute a backend. Keep LSFG private under the owner's beta
authorization; redistribution is a separate permission/release gate. A source-code
route does not prove working runtime support.

Each run binds source snapshot hashes (including dirty changes), APK hash, core and
backend binaries, device/GPU/driver/OS, display mode, ROM/title identity, checkpoint,
input replay, settings and verifier hashes. VersionCode alone is insufficient:
different recent APKs share version 3.2.16 / code 90.

Use moving normal, demanding and transition/occlusion scenes; cover native 20/30/60
image rates where available and special dual-screen paths. Begin with three
independent ten-minute runs per required configuration after bounded warmup,
including thermal/stress coverage. Retain all intervals from launch to shutdown.
Label loading separately; do not delete it. Any unexplained steady-motion long/short
scan hold or missed output fails that timing run. Guest-native stalls remain
observed stalls with separate attribution. A clean final epoch cannot erase failure.

Report every physical-present interval, expected scans, worst hold/phase error,
missing/repeated outputs, trace coverage and timing uncertainty. Calibrate precision
below a scan; a tool unable to resolve a missed scan cannot qualify pacing. Retired
guest ticks and emulated-time/wall-time must confirm the correction; audio queues
and A/V drift must agree. Check complete native-aspect image, orientation, screen
assignment, input/touch, suspend/resume and backend switching. Use full height where
compatible with original aspect and complete visibility; never stretch/crop to force
it. Offline math tests are not physical-device evidence.

First-stage checker:
[`verify_frame_generation_evidence_v2.py`](../tools/verify_frame_generation_evidence_v2.py).
It checks persisted identities, artifacts and trace structure, but deliberately
cannot return PASS. Well-formed declarations do not establish real pixel quality,
guest speed or scanout. It reports INVALID or UNVERIFIED until independent image,
physical-timing and review gates exist. Synthetic fixtures are not gameplay evidence.

## Device safety and completion

Use the Android-device-control skill, explicitly selecting the authorized serial
(Thor observed here: `427c87b2`). Both OLED panels stay black/off except during
bounded active tests. Arrange cleanup before waking: stop the test, sleep the device,
verify both actual brightness values are zero and check power state. Cleanup must
run after success, error, timeout or interruption. Never leave a static menu while
building/reviewing. Coordinate before interrupting another active test.

Do not complete the goal after planning, a build, a menu clip or one good game.
Completion requires evidence for the matrix gates and explicit owner review of
remaining unsupported cases/limitations.
